summary:
MGMT’s fourth album, *Little Dark Age*, was released on February 9, 2018, after more than four years without new material. The band began work again in late 2015, but struggled until producer Patrick Wimberly helped them loosen their process and collaborate with other musicians—including Ariel Pink, James Richardson, and Connan Mockasin. They later recorded with longtime producer Dave Fridmann, whose approach helped create a less abrasive sound.

The album’s title and songs reflect the band’s reaction to the political and social climate, particularly Donald Trump’s election, alongside more personal concerns. The artwork draws on illustrations from a 1988 horror zine and a work by Swiss artist Aloïse Corbaz. Four singles preceded the album, and MGMT launched its supporting tour in January 2018.

Critics generally responded positively, often describing the record as a return to the catchy, offbeat pop of *Oracular Spectacular*. Some reviewers, however, found it indecisive or short on ideas. The album earned a Metacritic score of 77 and reached No. 35 on the *Billboard* 200.

The artwork draws on multiple illustrations from the 1988 horror zine; the points identify only one illustration from that zine.
